question: According to Figure 4D-2, what are the general minimum and maximum longitudinal distances from the stop line for the primary signal faces, absent the near-side supplemental-face exception?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Figure 4D-2 shows that primary signal faces must be located no less than 40 feet beyond the stop line and no more than 180 feet beyond the stop line (the 180-foot maximum applies to 12-inch signal faces and may be exceeded only if a supplemental near-side signal face is provided). The figure also shows a shorter maximum of 120 feet from the stop line for 8-inch signal faces. Standards (mandatory): - Primary left-turn, right-turn, and at least one (preferably both) of the two required through-movement signal faces "shall be located: 1. No less than 40 feet beyond the stop line, and 2. No more than 180 feet beyond the stop line unless a supplemental near-side signal face is provided." - "The primary signal faces that are used to satisfy the requirements of Item A shall simultaneously satisfy the lateral placement requirement described in Section 4D.07 (see Figure 4D-2)." - Per Section 4D.07, the qualifying signal faces "shall be located between two lines intersecting with the center of the approach at a point 10 feet behind the stop line," each at approximately 20 degrees to the right and left of the center of the approach extended, and "shall simultaneously satisfy the longitudinal placement requirement described in Section 4D.08 (see Figure 4D-2)." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 4D-2 depicts the dimensioned placement zone with "40 ft*" labeled as the "Minimum distance of signal faces from stop line," "120 ft**" as the "Maximum distance from stop line for 8-inch signal face," and "180 ft***" as the "Maximum distance from stop line for 12-inch signal faces, unless a near-side supplemental signal face is used," measured within a wedge defined by 20° lines from a point 10 feet behind the stop line at the center of the approach. - [Image 2] Page 672 shows the same Figure 4D-2 in its full-page context with the footnote definitions of the 40-ft minimum and the 120-ft/180-ft maximums. - [Image 3] Page 673 shows Section 4D.08's Standard text requiring placement no less than 40 feet and no more than 180 feet beyond the stop line unless a supplemental near-side signal face is provided. - [Image 4] Page 671 shows Section 4D.07's Standard establishing the 20-degree lateral wedge from a point 10 feet behind the stop line that must be satisfied simultaneously with the longitudinal requirement. - [Image 5] Page 668 shows Section 4D.05, which the figure's Note 1 references for approaches with speeds of 45 mph or higher. Citations: - Section 4D.08 Standard §1 (p.673) - Section 4D.07 Standard §1 (p.671) - Section 4D.07 Option §7 (p.672) - Figure 4D-2 (p.672)
gold_answer: At least 40 feet and no more than 180 feet beyond the stop line.
